Dear Dr. Vance,

Thank you for seeing this 47-year-old woman in consultation for a comprehensive assessment and long-term surveillance strategy. She is currently feeling well, works as an accountant, and has no history of smoking or alcohol use. Her current medications are limited to daily vitamin D and an occasional ibuprofen for tension headaches.

Her medical history is notable for a localized renal clear-cell malignancy treated with a robotic-assisted partial nephrectomy two years ago, with recent cross-sectional imaging demonstrating a clear surgical bed. During a recent preventative health visit, a palpable fullness was noted in the anterior neck. A targeted ultrasound identified a discrete 1.7 cm solitary mass in the right thyroid lobe. A fine-needle aspiration was performed, which demonstrated benign follicular elements; thyroid carcinoma was explicitly excluded on the cytopathological review. 

On physical examination today, her blood pressure is 118/74 mmHg and pulse is 68 beats per minute. Cardiopulmonary and abdominal examinations were completely unremarkable. Dermatologic examination revealed multiple small, pedunculated cutaneous papillomatous growths distributed along the base of her neck and bilateral axillae. Bilateral screening mammography performed earlier this year was thoroughly reviewed and showed no evidence of breast carcinoma or suspicious microcalcifications. Her family history is non-contributory, with both parents living and healthy in their late seventies.

I would value your overall assessment and guidance regarding appropriate next steps or further surveillance for this patient.

Sincerely,
Dr. Marcus Croft
